osric_first_meet: ^A grey man at a folding table by the well turns a page in a ledger and doesn't look up until he's finished the line.
^"Osric Hale. Warden-Captain, Greyholt's watch, which is to say Lord Pellam's, which is to say mostly mine."

b: ^"You stand like the Company. I'll not ask. The Watch has taken worse than deserters, and I've signed for most of them."
^. Maudry said you'd be back. She says a lot. This time she was right."
^"Reedholm. Sister Ilse will want you. She wants everyone who can read, and gets about one a year."
^"Deepdelver boots. Good. The last pair I saw walked into the barrows and walked out again, which is more than the Watch manages."
^"Write your name in the book if you mean to stay. I like to know who to send the bill to."

s0: ^Osric marks something in the ledger and nods at the stool. "Sit if you like. It's the Watch's stool. Nobody else wants it."
s2: ^"The well's been quiet today. The well's always quiet. It's the barrows that aren't."

b: ^ "You've the look of three lines in my book. Let's have them."
^ "Three paid, three written. The Watch doesn't forget a debt, even when Greyholt does."
^ "The barrows road's open. I've written it in the ledger, under things Lord Pellam will take the credit for."
^ "Sister Ilse sent me a note. It says 'the fens.' Two words. She's never used two words for anything."
^ "Sister Ilse read me your tablets. A legion holding a road until relieved." He looks at the ledger for a long moment. "I know how that goes."

^ "Ilse says the order to stand down was written and never sent." He closes the ledger, which he never does. "Somebody should have sent it. That's all a Watch is, in the end. Somebody who sends the letter."

osric_greet_fallen: ^Osric looks at the space beside you where
^ should be, and writes something down.
^"I keep a page for the ones who don't come back up. Take
^ to the Shrine before I need it."
osric_topics: ^The Redhand are out of the mill.
osric_ledger_early: ^"For you? Not yet. The ones worth a bounty lead the walking kind, and they'd have you for breakfast."
^"Win a few rooms in the barrows first. Come back when your boots have seen the second floor."
osric_ledger_offer: ^"There's one kind worth paying for. Every fifth wave or so, one of them comes up with eyes like forge coals and the rest fall into step behind it."
^"They're the ones holding the second rank across the barrows road. Officers. Put enough of them down below and the rank on the road goes with them."
^"Put three of those down in the Old Barrows. Lord Pellam's coin is due any week now, which is what it said last month. Until it comes, I pay, and I write it down."

c-0: ^"Good. Don't go alone into the deep rooms. I've enough names on that page."
c-1: ^"The bright-eyed ones will keep. They've kept three hundred years."

osric_ledger_active: ^"Three of the bright-eyed ones. They lead every fifth wave. Stay in the room long enough and one will come to you."
^"And step out when you're low. A room doesn't care how brave you were."
osric_ledger_turnin: ^Osric counts on his fingers, then writes three short lines in the ledger and blots them.
^"Paid in full. Out of my purse, which Lord Pellam will repay, which is a sentence I have written before."
osric_ch1_report: ^Osric opens the ledger to a fresh page, which for him is a ceremony.
^"Out of the mill. Good. Where to?" He listens, and writes. "Wickham Keep. Of course. It has walls, and nobody's collected rent on it for three hundred years."
^"The Keep's on the Wickham road, north of the crossroads. The gate's been barred since spring. It won't be now, not to you. They'll want to see who knocked."
osric_ch2_offer: ^"The Redhand at Wickham Keep answer to a Captain Garrow. He collects. Tolls, tithes, debts, men who owe him."
^"Here's what I don't like. The carters say there's digging in the Keep's cellars. Bandits don't dig. Bandits take what somebody else dug up."
^"Somebody's paying them. I'd like to know who, and I'd like Garrow to stop collecting."

c-0: ^"Down to the second floor. That's where he'll be, counting. Take company,
^. Garrow doesn't fight alone. He never has."
c-1: ^"He's not going anywhere. That's rather the problem."

osric_ch2_active: ^"Wickham Keep, second floor. Garrow keeps his men close and his coin closer."
^"When he's in trouble he shouts, and they come. Put down the ones who come, then him. That's the whole of the tactics. It's usually enough."
osric_ch2_turnin: ^Osric reads the page you give him twice, then a third time, which is once more than he reads anything.
^"Garrow's own ledger. He kept books. Of course he did." He taps a line. "'For digging at the chapel, forty crowns. Ask no questions of the robes.' Robes."
^"Well. Garrow's done collecting. I'll write that down with some pleasure."
osric_ch3_offer: ^"The Sunken Chapel. In the marsh south of here, where the river's been eating it for a century."
^"Men in robes paid Garrow to dig there, and paid well, and asked for nothing up. Whatever they want is still down there. Or it was."
^"Find the one who pays. Ask him what for. If he won't say, stop him paying."

c-0: ^"It's older than the Keep and wetter than the barrows. Sister Ilse says it was a place where things were bound. She says it the way other people say 'haunted.'"
c-1: ^"The robes will keep digging. They don't strike me as the kind who stop for weather."

osric_ch3_active: ^"The Sunken Chapel. Mind your footing. The floor's the river's now."
^"Whatever you find on the one in charge, bring it back. Not to me. To Sister Ilse. I only write things down. She reads them."
osric_trial_offer: ^"I held a gate at Greyholt once. Nine days. They sent relief on the tenth, and apologised for the delay, which is more than most get."
^"Your fighter swings well enough. Swinging isn't the trick. Staying is. Go to Wickham Keep and hold, room after room, eight times, and don't give ground you don't have to."

c-0: ^"Eight waves. Then come back, and I'll show your fighters the one thing I know."
c-1: ^"The Keep will still have walls when you want them."

osric_trial_active: ^"Eight waves in Wickham Keep. It doesn't matter which rooms. It matters that you're still in them at the end."
osric_trial_turnin: ^Osric stands, which he does rarely, and takes the Watch's old shield down from behind his table.
^"Feet here. Shield here. Don't look at the blade, look at the one holding it. And when they come, let them. That's the whole of it. It took me nine days to learn."
osric_watch: ^"Greyholt sent a Captain and a man to hold Thornwick against the dead. I'm the Captain. Jory's the man."
^"We keep the book, we keep the well, and we keep people out of the barrows who've no business there. You've business there, so I'll not keep you."
osric_pellam: ^"Lord Pellam writes. Three pages to Thornwick last month, on good paper. Maudry read it twice. So did I."
^"It says he is aware, that he is concerned, and that help is being considered at the highest level. The highest level is him. He's considering it."

s0: ^"Mind the well. People fall in it more than you'd think."
s1: ^"Come back up. It's all I ask."
s2: ^Osric has already gone back to the ledger.
